gaps.sentence: He was sent to prison for ___ the law.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'the law' (opposite of obeying it)
gaps.explanation: break the law means to commit a crime; after the preposition 'for' the -ing form is needed.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a serious accident on his motorbike last year.
gaps.explanation: have an accident is the fixed collocation for being involved in one.

gaps.sentence: Most children learn to ___ the time before they start school.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the time (read a clock)
gaps.explanation: tell the time means to be able to read a clock; it is a fixed expression.

gaps.sentence: Who ___ the washing-up in your house?
gaps.explanation: do the washing-up means to wash the dishes; the -s form is needed with 'who'.

gaps.sentence: A true friend will always ___ a secret.
gaps.explanation: keep a secret is the fixed collocation for not telling it to anyone.

gaps.sentence: I only ___ sight of the celebrity for a second before the crowd closed in.
gaps.explanation: catch sight of somebody/something means to notice them briefly.

gaps.sentence: We ___ breakfast on the terrace every morning in summer.
gaps.explanation: have breakfast/lunch/dinner is the standard collocation for eating meals.

gaps.sentence: The poster in the shop window ___ my eye.
gaps.explanation: catch somebody's eye means to attract someone's attention.
